behavior_constraints: Strip all control characters (bytes below 0x20) except space (0x20) from user-supplied detail strings before storing in audit log entries
Truncate the sanitized (control-char-stripped) detail string to a maximum of 256 characters
Append the suffix '...[truncated]' when truncation occurs
Apply control character removal before truncation so the 256-char limit applies to the cleaned string
Use only Go standard library packages for the sanitization logic
Normal detail strings without control characters pass through unchanged

config.updated audit entry must continue to record the submitted configuration update payload as its detail (unmodified by the handler), so that long submitted values produce long detail strings subject to truncation
All existing audit actions and their recorded detail content must remain unchanged except for sanitization/truncation applied at storage time
entities.summary: Sanitize user-supplied detail strings in audit log entries by stripping control characters and truncating to 256 characters before storage.

instruction_head:
## Security Review: Unsanitized User Input in Audit Logs

User-supplied data is written directly into audit log entries without any sanitization. An attacker can inject control characters (carriage returns, null bytes, ANSI escape sequences) to perform log injection or confuse log parsers. Very long strings can flood audit logs and cause excessive memory usage, potentially leading to denial of service.
